### venturi3d {#sec-example-turbulence-venturi3d}

This example examines a steady flow in a Venturi tube.
A Venturi tube is a cylindrical tube, which has a reduced cross-section in the middle part.
At this constriction is an injection tube.
As a result of the accelerating fluid in the constriction, the static pressure decreases and the injection tube's fluid is pumped into the main tube.
The overall geometry is built by adding together single bodies, which are read from the XML file `venturi3d.xml`.
The example shows how to build a geometry from indicator functors and how to set the boundary conditions on it automatically.

#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I$ is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^3$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid with kinematic viscosity $\nu \in \R_{> 0}$ and constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= -\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p + \nu \Delta \vel \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I.
\end{align}
Along a streamline of a steady flow in which viscous effects are small, these equations reduce to Bernoulli's equation,
$$
    p + \frac{\rho}{2} |\vel|^2 = \text{const},
$$
which explains the Venturi effect: where the fluid accelerates in the constriction, its static pressure drops.

#### Boundary conditions

The boundary $\partial \Omega = \Gamma_D \cup \Gamma_\text{out} \cup \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ consists of the main inlet $\Gamma_D$ (MN 3) at $x = 5$, the outlet (MN 4) at $x = 195$ and the opening of the injection tube (MN 5) at $y = 5$, which together form $\Gamma_\text{out}$, and the walls $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ (MN 2) (@fig-venturi3d-geometry-2),
\begin{align}
    \vel &= (u_\text{in}(r, t), 0, 0)^\top \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_D \times \I, \\
    p &= 0 \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_\text{out} \times \I, \\
    \vel &= \mathbf{0} \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}} \times \I.
\end{align}
At the main inlet, a Poiseuille profile is imposed as a Dirichlet velocity boundary condition, whereas at the outlet and the minor inlet, a Dirichlet pressure condition is set by $p=0$ (i.e. $\rho=1$).
Whether the fluid enters or leaves through the opening of the injection tube is not prescribed, but follows from the pressure in the constriction.
The inflow profile
$$
    u_\text{in}(r, t) = s(t)\, u_\text{max} \left( 1 - \frac{r^2}{R^2} \right), \qquad s(t) = \tau^3 \left( 10 - 15 \tau + 6 \tau^2 \right), \quad \tau = \min\left( \frac{t}{0.8\, T}, 1 \right),
$$
is raised from rest with `PolynomialStartScale` during the first $80\,\%$ of the simulated time $T$, updated every $50$ time steps by `setTemporalValues()`.
`CirclePoiseuille3D` takes the centre and the radius $R = 18$ of the profile from the inlet cells (MN 3). Its peak velocity is the characteristic velocity of the unit converter, $2\,\mathrm{m/s}$, times the scaling factor that `setTemporalValues()` passes as the last argument, $\Delta x = 0.1$, so $u_\text{max} = 0.2\,\mathrm{m/s}$.
The fluid is initially at rest.

#### Domain

The geometry is built from cylinders and cones, `IndicatorCylinder3D` and `IndicatorCone3D` ([Building Simulation Domains with Geometry Primitive Functors](/content/03_geometry.qmd#sec-indicators)).
Each body's geometry is defined by certain points (position vectors) in the coordinate system and their radius.
A cone-shaped cylinder needs the center of the start and end circles as well as the radii.
`createMesh()` and `prepareGeometry()` read these bodies from the section `Geometry` of `venturi3d.xml` with `createIndicatorF3D()` and `createIndicatorCylinder3D()` ([XML Parameter Files](/content/07_input_output.qmd#sec-xmlparams)), and the union `IndicatorUnion3D` adds them together to the overall geometry, as in @lst-venturi3d-geometry.

::: {#lst-venturi3d-geometry}
```{.xml}
<Venturi>
    <IndicatorUnion3D>
        <IndicatorCylinder3D center1="5 50 50" center2="40 50 50" radius="20"/>
        <IndicatorCone3D center1="40 50 50" center2="80 50 50" radius1="20" radius2="10"/>
        <IndicatorCylinder3D center1="80 50 50" center2="120 50 50" radius="10"/>
        <IndicatorCone3D center1="120 50 50" center2="160 50 50" radius1="10" radius2="20"/>
        <IndicatorCylinder3D center1="160 50 50" center2="195 50 50" radius="20"/>
        <IndicatorCylinder3D center1="115 50 50" center2="115 25 50" radius="4"/>
        <IndicatorCone3D center1="115 25 50" center2="115 5 50" radius1="4" radius2="10"/>
    </IndicatorUnion3D>
</Venturi>
```
Definition of the geometry of the Venturi tube in `venturi3d.xml`. The sections `Inflow`, `Outflow0` and `Outflow1` define three further cylinders at the openings.
:::

@fig-venturi3d-geometry-2 visualizes the defined point positions and @fig-venturi3d-geometry-1 shows the computational geometry.
The main tube has the radius $20$, which narrows in the cone `co1` to the radius $10$ of the throat `cyl2` from $x = 80$ to $120$ and widens again in the diffuser `co2`.
The injection tube `cyl4` of radius $4$ branches off the throat at $x = 115$ and widens in the cone `co3` to the radius $10$ of its opening at $y = 5$.

![Schematic diagram visualizing the defined point positions for `venturi3d`.](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/venturi3d_geometry_2.png){#fig-venturi3d-geometry-2 width="70%"}

![Built geometry as used in simulation of example `venturi3d`.](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/venturi3d_geometry_1.png){#fig-venturi3d-geometry-1 width="70%"}

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid. `createMesh()` builds the mesh around the union with the spacing $1/N$ in the coordinates of `venturi3d.xml`, where the default resolution $N = 1$ resolves the throat diameter with $20$ cells. This gives $135\,000$ fluid cells in a mesh of $484\,000$ cells, with one cuboid per process.

The LBM collision operator is the regularized BGK operator [@latt-regularized:06], used as `RLBdynamics` ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), together with the D3Q19 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)). Compared with the BGK operator, it is more stable for relaxation times close to $1/2$ [@nathen:17]. The lattice uses the floating point type of the build configuration, `FLOATING_POINT_TYPE`.
The walls (MN 2) are treated with `BounceBack`, the inlet (MN 3) with `InterpolatedVelocity` and the outlet and the opening of the injection tube (MN 4, MN 5) with `InterpolatedPressure` ([Define Boundary Method](/content/06_initial_boundary.qmd#sec-defineBoundaryMethod)).

The corresponding lattice is defined inside the case definition in `venturi3d.cpp` as in @lst-venturi3d-case.

::: {#lst-venturi3d-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<
  NavierStokes, Lattice<FLOATING_POINT_TYPE, descriptors::D3Q19<>>
>;
```
Case definition for the `venturi3d` example.
:::

The parameters are given in @tbl-venturi3d-params.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Resolution` | $N$ | $1$ | cells per unit length of the geometry, and per characteristic length $L$ |
| `CharLatticeVelocity` | | $0.2$ | lattice velocity that corresponds to the characteristic velocity, sets $\Delta t$ |
| `CharPhysLength` | $L$ | $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ | characteristic length, sets $\Delta x = L / N$ |
| `CharPhysVelocity` | | $2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ | characteristic velocity |
| `PhysViscosity` | $\nu$ | $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$ | kinematic viscosity |
| `PhysDensity` | $\rho$ | $1\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ | density |
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | $T$ | $200\,\mathrm{s}$ | simulated time, $20\,000$ time steps |

: Parameters of `venturi3d`. `PHYS_MAX_T` is set in `main()`, all others in the section `Application` of `venturi3d.xml`. {#tbl-venturi3d-params}

#### Validation

`getResults()` prints the lattice statistics and writes the velocity and the pressure to `tmp/vtkData/venturi3d.pvd`, together with two heat maps of the velocity magnitude in the plane $z = 50$ through the axis of the tube (@fig-venturi3d-heatmap).
`SuperEuklidNorm3D` computes the magnitude of the velocity and `BlockReduction3D2D` samples it on the plane with the normal $(0, 0, 1)$ through the centre of the mesh. `heatmap::write()` writes the whole plane with the default settings and, with the parameters `heatmap::plotParam`, a second heat map named `outflow` with five contour levels and the colour map `blackbody`, zoomed to the region behind the throat ([Heatmap](/content/07_input_output.qmd#heatmap)).

::: {#fig-venturi3d-heatmap layout-ncol="1"}
![Default settings](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/heatmap/velocity_iT0019900.jpeg)

![`outflow`, zoomed with `zoomOrigin` $(0.6, 0.3)$ and `zoomExtend` $(0.4, 0.7)$, colour map `blackbody`](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/heatmap/outflow_iT0019900.jpeg)

Heat maps of the velocity magnitude in m/s of `venturi3d` in the plane $z = 50$ at $t = 199\,\mathrm{s}$, as written by `getResults()`. The axes show the coordinates of `venturi3d.xml`, which the labels give in m.
:::

@fig-venturi3d-velocity shows the steady flow.
The fluid accelerates in the cone `co1` and leaves the throat as a jet, which does not follow the widening walls of the diffuser `co2` but keeps its diameter up to the outlet, surrounded by slow fluid.
Fluid from the injection tube enters the main tube at the lower wall of the throat and is carried along with the jet.

![Velocity magnitude of `venturi3d` in the plane $z = 50$ at $t = 199\,\mathrm{s}$, with streamlines from the main inlet (grey) and from the opening of the injection tube (white), visualized in ParaView. The colour range is $[0, 0.65]\,\mathrm{m/s}$.](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/velocity/venturi3dVelocity.png){width="100%" #fig-venturi3d-velocity .lightbox}

@fig-venturi3d-centreline compares the static pressure on the axis of the tube with Bernoulli's equation.
From the inlet to the end of the throat, the static pressure falls from $0.169\,\mathrm{Pa}$ to its minimum of $-0.0145\,\mathrm{Pa}$ at $x = 122$, by $0.184\,\mathrm{Pa}$, while the velocity on the axis grows from $0.2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ to $0.634\,\mathrm{m/s}$, for which Bernoulli's equation gives the pressure drop $\tfrac{\rho}{2} (0.634^2 - 0.2^2)\,\mathrm{m^2/s^2} = 0.181\,\mathrm{Pa}$.
Accordingly, the total pressure $p + \tfrac{\rho}{2} u_x^2$ stays at $0.186\,\mathrm{Pa}$ within $3\,\%$ along the whole axis.
Since the jet does not slow down in the diffuser, the static pressure is not recovered behind the throat but stays close to the outlet pressure $p = 0$. The pressure at the junction of the injection tube is therefore only about $0.01\,\mathrm{Pa}$ below the pressure at its opening.

![Static, dynamic and total pressure of `venturi3d` on the axis $y = z = 50$ of the tube at $t = 199\,\mathrm{s}$, with the axial velocity $u_x$, evaluated in ParaView. The grey region marks the throat.](/examples/turbulence/venturi3d/doc/fig/pressure/centreline.svg){width="80%" #fig-venturi3d-centreline .lightbox}
